meaning: Control cannot read the outdoor sensor due to a short circuit. It assumes an outdoor temperature of 32 F (0 C) and continues operation. Clear after repair by pressing the Item button.
causes: Short circuit in the sensor wiring
Moisture in the sensor
Defective sensor
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

Measure the actual temperature at the sensor, then measure the sensor resistance and compare with the resistance chart (256 manual p.12; 274 manual refers to Data Brochure D 070). 10 kOhm NTC at 77 F.
Very high resistance: broken wire, poor connection or defective sensor. Very low resistance: shorted wiring, moisture in the sensor or defective sensor.
Measure directly at the sensor location to isolate the sensor from the wiring.

meaning: Control cannot read the outdoor sensor due to an open circuit. It assumes an outdoor temperature of 32 F (0 C) and continues operation. Clear after repair by pressing the Item button.
causes: Broken wire
Poor wiring connection
Defective sensor
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

Measure directly at the sensor location to isolate the sensor from the wiring.

causes: Short circuit in the sensor wiring
Moisture in the sensor
Defective sensor
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

Defective sensor

meaning: Control could not read a piece of information from its EEPROM. It loads factory defaults and stops operation until all settings are verified.
causes: Noisy power source
checks: Verify all settings in the Adjust menu.
Check the quality of the 24 V power supply.

causes: Short circuit in the sensor wiring
Moisture in the sensor
Defective sensor
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

Measure the actual temperature at the sensor, then measure the sensor resistance and compare with the resistance chart (256 manual p.12; 274 manual refers to Data Brochure D 070). 10 kOhm NTC at 77 F.
Very high resistance: broken wire, poor connection or defective sensor. Very low resistance: shorted wiring, moisture in the sensor or defective sensor.
Measure directly at the sensor location to isolate the sensor from the wiring.

causes: Broken wire
Poor wiring connection
Defective sensor
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

meaning: Control failed to read the boiler supply sensor due to a short circuit. With a call for heat it no longer controls the boiler(s); it provides a boiler enable to the boiler aquastat or control until repaired. It will not operate the boiler contact if Boil Minimum is below 100 F (38 C). Self clears when corrected.
causes: Short circuit in the sensor wiring
Moisture in the sensor
Defective sensor
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

Measure the actual temperature at the sensor, then measure the sensor resistance and compare with the resistance chart (256 manual p.12; 274 manual refers to Data Brochure D 070). 10 kOhm NTC at 77 F.
Very high resistance: broken wire, poor connection or defective sensor. Very low resistance: shorted wiring, moisture in the sensor or defective sensor.
Measure directly at the sensor location to isolate the sensor from the wiring.

meaning: Control failed to read the boiler supply sensor due to an open circuit. It no longer controls the boiler; it provides a boiler enable to the boiler aquastat or control until repaired. It will not operate the boiler contact if Boil Minimum is below 100 F (38 C). Self clears when corrected.
causes: Broken wire
Poor wiring connection
Defective sensor
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

Measure the actual temperature at the sensor, then measure the sensor resistance and compare with the resistance chart (256 manual p.12; 274 manual refers to Data Brochure D 070). 10 kOhm NTC at 77 F.
Very high resistance: broken wire, poor connection or defective sensor. Very low resistance: shorted wiring, moisture in the sensor or defective sensor.
Measure directly at the sensor location to isolate the sensor from the wiring.
If the supply sensor was removed deliberately, power the control down for 10 seconds, then restart it.

meaning: Communication lost on the Boiler Bus due to a short or open circuit.
causes: Short or open circuit on the tN4 bus
Reversed C and R polarity
Loose or broken wires
checks: Check the tN4, C and R wires for each tN4 device.
Check the polarity of the C and R wires.
Check for loose or broken wires.

meaning: Control failed to read the Adjust Menu settings and reloaded factory defaults. Operation stops until all Adjust Menu settings are checked.
checks: Set the access level to Advanced and check all settings in the Adjust menu to clear the error.

meaning: More than one tN4 device has been assigned the same master number.
causes: Duplicate schedule master number on the network
checks: Reassign master numbers so each tN4 device has a unique one.

meaning: The control failed to read the Time menu settings and reloaded the factory defaults. Operation continues normally.
causes: Time menu settings could not be read
checks: Set the access level to Advanced and check the settings in the Time menu to clear the error.

meaning: The control failed to read the Schedule menu settings and reloaded the factory defaults. Operation continues normally.
causes: Schedule menu settings could not be read
checks: Set the access level to Advanced and check the settings in the Schedule menu to clear the error.

meaning: The control failed to read the Miscellaneous menu settings and reloaded the factory defaults. Operation continues normally.
causes: Miscellaneous menu settings could not be read
checks: Set the access level to Advanced and check the settings in the Miscellaneous menu to clear the error.

meaning: Communication is lost to a tN4 device on the boiler bus. The number shown is the address of the lost device.
causes: No power to the lost device
Loose or damaged wiring to the device
checks: Ensure there is power to the lost device (its LCD shows Bus Boil OPn).
Trace the wires from the control to the lost device for loose or damaged wires.
The message clears itself when corrected; if a device was deliberately removed, hold the Up and Down buttons to clear it.

meaning: More than one tN4 System control has been detected on the tN4 bus.
causes: Two tN4 buses wired together
checks: Check the tN4 bus wiring. The error clears once the condition is corrected.

meaning: The selected system schedule is no longer available.
causes: The system schedule master is no longer connected to the network
The system schedule number was changed on the schedule master
checks: Restore the schedule master connection or schedule number. The error clears when corrected.

meaning: A device on the boiler bus has an error; the address shown (b:01 to b:24) is the device with the error.
causes: Error at the device with the displayed address
checks: Go to the device with the displayed address and read its error.

meaning: The control failed to read the DHW sensor due to a short circuit, so it no longer heats the DHW tank.
causes: Short in the DHW sensor or its wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070. DHW heating resumes and the message clears once corrected.

meaning: The control failed to read the DHW sensor due to an open circuit, so it no longer heats the DHW tank.
causes: Open in the DHW sensor or its wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070. DHW heating resumes and the message clears once corrected.

meaning: Both primary pump P1 and P2 have failed.
causes: Both primary pumps failed to prove
checks: Check both pumps and their proof devices.

meaning: The Prim P1 relay closed but a flow proof demand was not detected before the proof demand delay elapsed.
causes: Pump P1 or its flow proof device failed
checks: Check pump P1 and its flow proof wiring and device.

meaning: The Prim P2 relay closed but a flow proof demand was not detected before the proof demand delay elapsed.
causes: Pump P2 or its flow proof device failed
checks: Check pump P2 and its flow proof wiring and device.

meaning: The primary pump has been turned off but the pump proof demand remains after 4 minutes.
causes: Pump proof demand still present after the pump was turned off
checks: Check the pump proof device and its wiring.

meaning: The C.A. relay closed but the control did not detect a damper proof demand before the proof demand delay elapsed.
causes: Combustion air damper or its proof device failed
checks: Check the damper, its proof switch and wiring.

meaning: The combustion air damper has been turned off but the damper proof demand remains after 4 minutes.
causes: Damper proof demand still present after the damper was turned off
checks: Check the damper proof device and its wiring.

meaning: The control failed to read the boiler return sensor due to a short circuit; it continues to operate normally.
causes: Short in the return sensor or wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070. The message clears once corrected.

meaning: The control failed to read the boiler return sensor due to an open circuit; it continues to operate normally.
causes: Open in the return sensor or wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070. The message clears once corrected.

meaning: The boiler supply temperature did not increase within the boiler alarm time.
causes: No temperature rise at the boiler supply sensor within the alarm time
checks: To reset the alarm, press and hold the Up and Down buttons for 5 seconds while viewing the error message.

meaning: A DHW sensor and a DHW demand have been applied at the same time. The DHW tank will not be heated until the demand signal is removed.
causes: Externally powered DHW demand applied while the DHW sensor is enabled
checks: Remove the powered DHW demand or disable the DHW sensor. The message clears once the condition is corrected.

meaning: The control was unable to read a piece of information from its EEPROM. It loads the factory defaults and stops operation until all the settings are verified.
causes: Noisy power source
checks: Verify all settings in the control.

meaning: The control cannot read the outdoor sensor due to a short circuit. It assumes an outdoor temperature of 32 F (0 C) and continues operation.
causes: Short in the outdoor sensor or wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070.
To clear the error after repair, press the Item button.

meaning: The control cannot read the outdoor sensor due to an open circuit. It assumes an outdoor temperature of 32 F (0 C) and continues operation.
causes: Open in the outdoor sensor or wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070.
To clear the error after repair, press the Item button.

meaning: The control cannot read the mixing supply sensor. It operates the mixing valve at a fixed output as long as there is a mixing demand.
causes: Short or open circuit in the mixing supply sensor or wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070.
To clear the error after repair, press the Item button.

meaning: The control cannot read the boiler sensor due to a short circuit. If BOIL MIN is above 100 F (38 C) it closes the Boiler contact when the mixing valve starts to operate; the boiler temperature is then limited by the operating aquastat. If BOIL MIN is below 100 F it does not operate the Boiler contact.
causes: Short in the boiler sensor or wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070.
To clear the error after repair, press the Item button.

meaning: The control cannot read the boiler sensor due to an open circuit. If BOIL MIN is above 100 F (38 C) it closes the Boiler contact when the mixing valve starts to operate; the boiler temperature is then limited by the operating aquastat. If BOIL MIN is below 100 F it does not operate the Boiler contact.
causes: Open in the boiler sensor or wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 070.
If the sensor was deliberately removed, power the control down and back up.
To clear the error after repair, press the Item button.

meaning: The control cannot read the indoor sensor. It continues to operate as if nothing were connected to the indoor sensor input.
causes: Short or open circuit in the indoor sensor or wiring
checks: Locate and repair the problem as described in Data Brochure D 074.
If the sensor was deliberately removed, power down and back up.
To clear the error after repair, press the Item button.

meaning: The control enclosure has overheated or the control has an internal error. The control stops operation until the condition is corrected.
causes: Enclosure overheating
Internal error
checks: Try resetting by powering down, waiting 1 minute and powering back up.
